The fix is **PR #1943** ("(fix) O3-6093: Improve support for arrow functions in expression variable extractor", by ibacher), merged as commit `cd6cf1fcbdab85d05529d015dfb911dfef885b84`. It makes the extractor carry the enclosing arrow-function parameters into the arrow body, so only identifiers that are still unbound get reported. The PR body says unbound variables in arrow bodies such as `() => !x` were not captured.

The implementation lives in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-expression-evaluator/src/extractor.ts`:
- `visitArrowFunctionExpression` (lines 111-120) copies the context's `boundNames`, adds the arrow's identifier parameters, and visits the body with that set. The old behaviour dropped the body's identifiers, which is why `a.map(x => f(b))` yielded only `a`.
- `visitIdentifier` (lines 150-154) adds a name to `variables` only if it is not a global and not in `boundNames`.
- The `EvaluationContext` interface (lines 159-164) gains the `boundNames` field that makes this work.

Regression tests are in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-expression-evaluator/src/extractor.test.ts`. The new cases at lines 50-57 cover arrow bodies such as `a.map(x => f(b))`, and lines 59-68 cover parameter exclusion, nested arrows and scope limits. The PR also adds a changeset, `openmrs-esm-core/.changeset/flat-mammals-fail.md`.

I did not open the PR's diff, so I have not seen the exact pre-fix code that the 34 deleted lines removed. The line references above are from the merged file at the merge commit.
